title: It Started With a Letter — Chapter 1
body:
I made this website a long time ago. Back then, everything was handwritten. It all started when you told me it was the first time someone had ever given you handwritten letters.

For some reason, that little detail stayed with me. And then, I had a clever idea.

What if I made something that could hold more than just a few letters? Somewhere I could put my thoughts into words, keep little memories, and leave you something you could come back to whenever you felt like reading.

title: It Started With a Letter — Chapter 2
body:
Do you remember that time I showed up with halo-halo when you were having a rough day? There was a letter hidden inside it, and behind the note, I wrote, "Bayaran mo yan."

That was the letter I meant. The one that came with the halo-halo, with a little joke written behind it. I was teasing you, obviously, but I also wanted to do something thoughtful for you. Something small that might make a difficult day a little better.

I didn't really meant the "bayaran mo yan" part. Bintahi.

title: It Started With a Letter — Chapter 3
body:
Looking back, it's funny how that one handwritten letter became part of the reason I wanted to make this website.

I started thinking about how I could give you more than a single note, more than a moment you might eventually forget. I wanted to make somewhere I could leave you little pieces of my thoughts, memories, and things I don't always say out loud.

Something you could return to whenever you wanted, without needing to keep a stack of handwritten papers safe somewhere.

title: It Started With a Letter — Chapter 4
body:
And now, here we are. A whole notebook, all because you once told me something as simple as never having received handwritten letters before.

I don't know if you realized how much that little detail would stick with me. Maybe you were just sharing something about yourself, and I was sitting there quietly turning it into an idea in my head.

Apparently, that's what happens when you tell me something. Sometimes I listen. Sometimes I remember. And sometimes I turn it into an entire project.

title: It Started With a Letter — Chapter 5
body:
This website isn't made of paper, and you won't find my handwriting on these pages. But the thought behind it is pretty similar to that first letter.

I wanted to give you something personal. Something made with you in mind, filled with memories, little reminders, random thoughts, and words I might not always find the right moment to say out loud.

Maybe it's a little unconventional to turn that idea into a website, but making things has always been one way I know how to express myself.

title: It Started With a Letter — Chapter 6
body:
So, if you ever wondered why I made this, that's the story.

It started with you telling me you'd never received handwritten letters before. It continued with a letter tucked inside some halo-halo, with "Bayaran mo yan" written behind it. And somewhere along the way, that small idea grew into this notebook.

One little conversation, one handwritten letter, and one questionable joke later, you ended up with an entire website.

Bintahi. You really had no idea what you were starting when you told me that story.

Anyway, I hope this notebook makes you smile whenever you read it. That's all I really wanted from the beginning.

title: A Little Reminder Before the Next Chapter
body:
Before you move on to the next chapter, take a little moment here. No need to rush through everything, bintahi. This notebook isn't going anywhere.

Every page has its own little story, and there's no deadline for reading them all. Take your time, smile at the silly parts, and keep the ones that mean something to you.

And if you ever forget where you left off, consider this your reminder: you still have more pages to read. Sus, may assignment ka pa pala.

title: The Chapter Began With One Cast — Chapter 1
body:
I just remembered one of the most unforgettable moments we had. The time I brought you and our friend to my fishing spot and decided to teach you how to cast a fishing rod.

I thought it would be a simple little fishing trip. I'd show you how to cast, you'd give it a try, and maybe we'd catch some fish along the way. A pretty reasonable plan, right? Well, apparently, I forgot to account for one very important possibility.

Your very first cast.

The fish were safe that day. Our friend, however, wasn't.

First cast: zero fish caught, one friend caught. Congratulations. You managed to catch something without even getting near the water the way you were supposed to. Bintahi, not exactly what you were aiming for, was it?

title: The Chapter Began With One Cast — Chapter 2
body:
What makes that moment unforgettable isn't just what happened. It's the fact that it was your very first attempt at casting a fishing rod, and somehow, it immediately became a memory worth keeping.

I was supposed to be teaching you how to fish, not introducing you to a completely different kind of target practice. Our friend probably didn't expect to become part of the lesson either.

But that's what made it funny. We went there to fish, and instead, we got a story that still deserves to be written down. The fish went about their day in peace, while our friend became an accidental part of fishing history.

I don't even know what the official fishing record is for catching a friend on the first cast, but I'm pretty sure you made a strong case for it.

title: The Chapter Began With One Cast — Chapter 3
body:
Looking back, I'm glad I got to share that little experience with you. It wasn't some big planned event or a perfect day where everything went according to plan. It was just us at my fishing spot, me trying to teach you something new, and one cast that went somewhere nobody expected.

Maybe you didn't catch a fish that day, but you definitely left with a story. And honestly, I'd say that's a pretty memorable first attempt.

So whenever you think about learning how to fish, remember the important lesson: watch where the rod is pointing before you cast. The fish aren't the only ones who deserve to feel safe around you.

And to our friend, wherever you are, I'm sorry your role in this memory is permanent. You were supposed to come fishing, not become the catch. Bintahi.

title: When Are We Fishing Again?
body:
I just realized we haven't gone fishing together in a while. I wonder when we'll get to do that again. Remember when I brought you and our friend to my fishing spot and tried teaching you how to cast a rod?

Your first cast was something else. Zero fish caught, one friend caught. Bintahi, we went there to catch fish, not our friend. I don't think I'll ever forget that.

It's been a while since that day, and it'd be fun to go fishing again sometime. Maybe we can visit the same spot or try somewhere new. Hopefully, you've improved your casting skills by then. For everyone's safety, especially our friend's.

Anyway, I was just wondering when we'll go again. We should plan another fishing trip when we get the chance. This time, let's try to catch actual fish.

title: That Day in July — Chapter 1
body:
I remember in July when you told me that it was going to be your last week staying there.

Then, while you were preparing to leave, something went wrong. You accidentally transferred the money to the wrong person, and you didn't know what to do about it.

You ended up calling me and telling me what happened.

title: That Day in July — Chapter 2
body:
I still remember that whole situation, especially because it all happened during what was supposed to be your last week there.

And that's not even the whole story...

Then came the worst part. Your supposed ''last week'' kept getting extended for several more weeks. You were completely exhausted and stressed, and there were nights when you cried until morning.

title: That Day in July — Chapter 3
body:
It was painful watching you go through so much when all you wanted was for everything to finally be over.

And just when you thought things couldn't get any more complicated, the money transfer happened again.

Every time you said, “This is my last week,” it somehow felt like another tragedy was waiting around the corner.

title: That Day jn July — Chapter 4
body:
Then you accidentally sent ₱1,500 to the wrong person.

At that point, I swear, “this is my last week” had stopped sounding like an update and started sounding like a warning.

Every time you said it, I was probably thinking, What is going to happen this time?

title: That Day in July — Chapter  5
body:
Looking back, the whole situation was stressful, exhausting, and honestly a little unbelievable.

I know it wasn't funny while you were going through it, especially with all the crying and worrying.

But it's one of those memories from July that I don't think I'll forget anytime soon.

And that's the part where you borrowed money from me.

title: You Don't Have to Figure It Out Alone — Chapter 1
body:
And that's how you ended up borrowing money from me.

But honestly, when I look back on that moment, I don't just remember the money or everything that went wrong that July.

I remember that you reached out to me when you didn't know what else to do.

title: You Don't Have to Figure It Out Alone — Chapter 2
body:
I'm glad you felt you could come to me during a difficult time.

I know I couldn't magically fix everything you were going through, but if I could help make things a little easier for you, even in a small way, then I'm glad I could be there.

Maybe that's one of the things friendship is about.

title: You Don't Have to Figure It Out Alone — Chapter 3
body:
Not always having the right answers or being able to solve every problem, but being someone you can turn to when life gets overwhelming.

And if there's one thing I hope you remember from that whole experience, it's that you don't always have to figure everything out on your own.

Sometimes, it's okay to ask for help. And I'm glad you trusted me enough to ask.

title: A Debt You Never Owed — Chapter 1
body:
Remember that time when you were having a rough day, and I showed up with halo-halo, with a letter hidden inside it?

And behind the note, I wrote, “Bayaran mo yan.”

Funny how that little joke became even more relevant later, when you actually had to borrow money from me.

title: A Debt You Never Owed — Chapter 2
body:
Back then, I wrote those words just to tease you. But when July came around and everything seemed to be going wrong, you really did end up needing my help.

First, there was the money you accidentally sent to the wrong person, then all the stress of trying to leave, and eventually, the ₱1,500 you accidentally sent to the wrong person again.

And somewhere in the middle of all that chaos, you came to me and borrowed money.

title: A Debt You Never Owed — Chapter 3
body:
So maybe, in a way, you finally got to “bayaran mo yan” that joke.

But honestly, I never wanted you to feel like you had to repay me for being there for you.

I helped because you needed help, and because you're my friend. That's it.

title: A Debt You Never Owed — Chapter 4
body:
The halo-halo, the letter, and the teasing might seem like separate little memories, but to me, they all carry the same meaning.

Whether you were having a rough day and needed something sweet, or going through a difficult time and needed someone to lean on, I wanted you to know that you could come to me.

title: A Debt You Never Owed — Chapter 5
body:
So yes, bayaran mo yan. Bintahi.

But if there's one thing you never have to pay back, it's the kindness I give you as your friend. That was never a debt.

I just hope that whenever life gets difficult, you remember you don't always have to face it alone.

title: You Went Quiet, And I Noticed — Chapter 1
body:
But honestly, beneath that assumption, I was wondering if you were okay.

I know you have your own things going on, and I don't expect you to tell me every little detail about your day.

Still, when someone I'm used to hearing from suddenly goes quiet, I notice.

title: You Went Quiet, And I Noticed — Chapter 2
body:
I wondered how your night was going, whether something happened, or if you were just tired and needed some time to yourself.

I didn't want to assume anything was wrong, but I couldn't help caring enough to wonder.

Maybe you were just busy. Maybe you fell asleep. Maybe you really were out there causing trouble. Any of those would be very on-brand for you.

title: You Went Quiet, And I Noticed — Chapter 3
body:
I just hope you were okay last night.

You don't always have to explain yourself to me, and you don't have to be in a good mood every time we talk.

But if something is bothering you, or if you're having one of those nights when everything feels a little heavier than usual, you don't have to pretend you're fine around me.

title: You Went Quiet, And I Noticed — Chapter 4
body: And if you were simply being a menace somewhere, then please continue your nonsense responsibly. I'd still rather hear that you were okay than find myself wondering whether you weren't.

title: A Softer Start to Your Day — Chapter 1
body:
Rise and shine. I hope you woke up smiling, feeling rested and calm, with a little less weight on your shoulders today.

I hope you slept well and that whatever was on your mind last night feels a little easier to carry this morning.

You deserve mornings that don't immediately ask too much of you, days that give you room to breathe, and little moments that remind you life isn't always as exhausting as it sometimes feels.

title: A Softer Start to Your Day — Chapter 2
body:
I hope something makes you smile today, even if it's something small.

Maybe a good meal, a funny message, or some random nonsense that makes you laugh when you least expect it.

And if you didn't wake up feeling your best, that's okay, too. You don't have to force yourself to be cheerful just because it's a new day. Take your time, breathe, and ease into it at your own pace.

title: A Softer Start to Your Day — Chapter 3
body:
Just a little reminder from me: I'm rooting for you, even on the ordinary days when nothing particularly special happens.

Now get up, sleepyhead. The world is waiting, unfortunately, and you still have nonsense to get into.

And if you're still sleepy, go back to sleep for a bit. Just don't blame me when you wake up and half the day is gone. Knowing you, you'd probably sleep through everything and still complain about being tired.

title: You're Allowed to Let It Out — Chapter 1
body:
I hope you know that crying doesn't make you weak.

Sometimes, things get too heavy, and you can't keep everything bottled up forever. You can try to be strong, tell yourself you're fine, and keep going like nothing bothers you, but that doesn't mean you have to hold everything in.

You've been crying since the day you were born. Before you could even speak, it was one of the ways you let the world know you were here. So why should it be something to be ashamed of now?

title: You're Allowed to Let It Out — Chapter 2
body:
You don't always have to be the strong one. You don't have to explain every tear or pretend you're okay when you're not.

If something hurts, let yourself feel it. If you need to cry, cry. You can take your time putting yourself back together.

And please remember that you don't have to go through every difficult moment alone. You don't need to hide the parts of yourself that are hurting just to make other people believe you're doing fine.

title: You're Allowed to Let It Out — Chapter 3
body:
You're human. You're allowed to have bad days, to feel overwhelmed, and to fall apart sometimes.

Crying doesn't mean you've given up. Sometimes, it simply means you've been holding on for a long time.

So be gentle with yourself, okay? You deserve the same kindness you give to everyone else. And if you ever need someone to listen, you don't have to pretend you're okay around me.

title: Because It Was With You — Chapter 1
body:
One completely honest sentence I never had the courage or opportunity to say is this: There are things I remember because they happened with you, and I don't think I would remember them the same way otherwise.

It's strange how that works. Sometimes, the moment itself isn't anything extraordinary. It's just an ordinary day, a random conversation, or something that probably seemed insignificant at the time.

But somehow, when I look back on it, the fact that you were there makes it worth remembering.

title: Because It Was With You — Chapter 2
body:
I think some memories become special because of the person we share them with.

Maybe I wouldn't remember the exact words someone else said, or what happened on an ordinary afternoon. But when it comes to certain moments with you, little details tend to stick around longer than I expect them to.

It's not always about what happened. Sometimes, it's simply that you were there, and that was enough to make the moment feel different.

title: Because It Was With You — Chapter 3
body:
I don't know if you remember those moments the same way I do. Maybe some of them have already slipped your mind, and that's okay. We don't always carry the same memories with us.

But I wanted you to know that some of the ordinary moments we've shared have stayed with me. Not because they were perfect or because something life-changing happened, but because they became little pieces of a friendship that means something to me.

And I think that's what makes them special. If those same moments had happened with someone else, they probably wouldn't mean quite the same thing.

They happened with you. That's why I remember.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 1
body:
A memory I hope you remember too is one where neither of us was trying to impress the other.

There is something nice about remembering people as they actually were instead of only remembering the polished versions.

Not the version of ourselves we show when we're trying to look good, say the right things, or make sure nobody sees our awkward side. Just us, being ourselves without thinking too much about it.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 2
body:
I think those are some of the best moments in a friendship. When you don't have to think carefully about every word you say or worry about how the other person might see you.

You can be weird, make questionable jokes, talk about absolutely nothing, or say something embarrassing without feeling like you have to recover your dignity immediately.

Not every conversation has to be deep, and not every moment has to become a special memory. Sometimes, it's enough to sit around, talk nonsense, and let the time pass.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 3
body:
What I like about those moments is that nobody has to pretend. You don't have to be in a good mood all the time, have everything figured out, or come up with something interesting to say.

You can be tired, quiet, distracted, or completely ridiculous, and the moment can still be worth remembering.

I think there's something comforting about being around someone without constantly feeling the need to prove that you're worth their time.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 4
body:
Maybe we don't remember every detail of those days. Maybe we wouldn't even agree on which moments were the most memorable.

But I hope there's at least one memory you can look back on and remember how natural everything felt. No pressure to impress each other, no need to make the moment bigger than it was, and no pretending to be someone we weren't.

Just two people sharing a little piece of their lives, probably talking about something completely unserious.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 5
body:
I hope when you think of me, you don't only remember the things I said when I was trying to be thoughtful or the times I tried to do something nice for you.

I hope you remember the ordinary version of me, too. The random conversations, the stupid jokes, the times I probably annoyed you, and all the little moments that didn't seem important at the time.

Because that's the version of our friendship I value most. Not something perfect or carefully put together, but something real.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 6
body:
And I hope you let yourself be remembered that way, too.

You don't have to be the funniest person in the room, the strongest person anyone knows, or the person who always has everything under control. You don't have to make yourself more interesting just to leave an impression.

The imperfect, unfiltered version of you is worth knowing, too. Even the version who gets tired, overthinks things, makes mistakes, and occasionally becomes a menace for absolutely no reason.

title: The Way We Really Were — Chapter 7
body:
I guess what I'm trying to say is that I hope we never feel like we have to turn our friendship into something impressive just to make it meaningful.

Some of the best things about knowing someone happen when neither person is trying to create a memory. You just spend time together, go through ordinary days, laugh at ridiculous things, and somehow end up with moments you carry long after they've passed.

Those are the memories I hope stay with you, too. Not because everything was perfect, but because, for a little while, we could simply be ourselves around each other.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 1
body:
You probably don't realize how often the little things you do make me smile.

Sometimes it's something funny you say, a random thought you decide to share, or the way you turn an ordinary conversation into something unexpectedly entertaining.

They're usually small moments, nothing worth making a big deal out of. But every now and then, I find myself remembering them later and smiling all over again.

And no, I'm not going to tell you exactly which moments. I have a reputation to maintain.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 2
body:
One thing I've come to appreciate about our conversations is that they don't always need a reason.

We don't have to discuss something important or come up with something interesting to say every time. Sometimes we just talk, share random nonsense, or tease each other over the smallest things.

And somehow, those conversations can be just as memorable as the serious ones.

I think there's something nice about having someone you can talk to without needing to plan what to say first.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 3
body:
Sometimes, I'll remember something you said hours or even days later, and suddenly it becomes funny all over again.

Meanwhile, you've probably forgotten the entire conversation and moved on with your life. Meanwhile, my brain has decided this particular moment deserves a replay.

Bintahi. Imagine being unintentionally entertaining enough to become a recurring thought in someone else's head.

Don't let that go to your head, though. I refuse to encourage you.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 4
body:
But it's not always about the funny things.

Sometimes, I appreciate the little things you share without realizing they matter. A random update about your day, something that's been bothering you, or a small detail you could've easily kept to yourself.

Those moments remind me that friendship isn't built only through big gestures or unforgettable events. Sometimes, it grows through ordinary conversations and the small pieces of life people choose to share with each other.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 5
body:
I hope you know that you don't have to do anything special to make your presence matter.

You don't have to be funny every day, always have something interesting to say, or constantly find ways to make people happy. You can have quiet days, boring conversations, and moments when you don't feel like doing much at all.

I'm not expecting you to be entertaining. Although, somehow, you manage to be funny without even trying sometimes.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 6
body:
I think that's what makes these memories feel genuine. They weren't carefully planned, and neither of us was trying to create something worth remembering.

We were just being ourselves. Talking about whatever came to mind, laughing at things that probably wouldn't make sense to anyone else, and making ordinary moments a little less ordinary.

Maybe we won't remember every conversation years from now, but I hope a few of those little moments stay with us.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 7
body:
If I ever seem to remember the smallest details about something you said, it's probably because those moments stayed with me longer than I expected.

Not because you need to read too much into it, and not because every little thing has some hidden meaning. Sometimes, a memory is simply nice to have.

And some memories are nice because they're connected to people we're glad to know.

You're one of those people for me.

title: The Little Things That Make Me Smile — Chapter 8
body:
So here's one thing I wanted to put into words: I'm glad our friendship has room for all these little moments.

The random conversations, the teasing, the unexpected jokes, the occasional serious talks, and even the moments when one of us says something so questionable that the other has to pause and reconsider the friendship.

Bintahi. I'm kidding. Mostly.

But really, thank you for being part of these memories. You might see them as ordinary moments, but some of them have made my days better in ways you probably never noticed.

And I think that's worth telling you, at least once.

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 1
body:
Something I'm grateful for is being able to have conversations with you that don't need to accomplish anything.

Sometimes we talk about the most random things, jump from one topic to another, or spend time saying absolutely nothing important. There's no particular reason for the conversation, no goal we're trying to reach, and no need to make every message meaningful.

And honestly, I think that's one of the nice things about having you as a friend. We don't always need a reason to talk. Sometimes, talking is enough.

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 2
body:
I think there's a kind of comfort in being able to talk to someone without constantly wondering what to say next.

We can joke around, share random thoughts, complain about something small, or talk about things that probably won't matter by tomorrow. Not every conversation has to turn into advice, a serious discussion, or some life-changing realization.

Sometimes, we just want to share a thought with someone and see where the conversation goes.

And somehow, even the most pointless conversations can become the ones we remember.

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 3
body:
Maybe that's why I appreciate those ordinary conversations more than I usually admit.

There's no pressure to be interesting all the time. I don't have to come up with something clever, and you don't have to have some amazing story to tell me. We can just talk about whatever comes to mind.

And if the conversation gets ridiculous, well, that's hardly a surprise with us.

Bintahi, sometimes we start with one topic and end up somewhere that makes absolutely no sense. How does that even happen?

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 4
body:
The thing is, spending time with someone doesn't always mean doing something special together.

Sometimes, it's just checking in, exchanging a few messages, or sharing something that reminded you of the other person. Even a short conversation can make an ordinary day feel a little less ordinary.

You might not think much of those moments because they happen so naturally. But I think there's something meaningful about being able to share the little, uneventful parts of life with someone.

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 5
body:
I don't expect every conversation we have to be memorable, and I don't expect us to always have something to say.

There will be busy days, quiet days, and times when neither of us feels like talking much. That's normal. A friendship doesn't have to be constantly entertaining to be worth keeping.

I'm just grateful for the times when we do get to talk, whether it's about something important or something so random that I wonder how we even got there.

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 6
body:
Maybe one day, we'll forget most of the things we talked about. The random jokes, the little complaints, the stories that seemed important for five minutes, and all the nonsense in between.

But I hope we remember how easy it could feel to share those moments. How we didn't always need a plan or a reason. How an ordinary conversation could simply be a nice part of an ordinary day.

Because sometimes, the point isn't what we talked about. It's that we got to spend a little time talking to each other.

title: Conversations That Didn't Need a Purpose — Chapter 7
body:
So, thank you for all the conversations that didn't need a purpose.

For the random messages, the unnecessary teasing, the unexpected topics, and even the conversations where neither of us had anything particularly interesting to contribute.

I'm glad we didn't need every moment to be special for it to mean something.

And if you ever think you're bothering me by telling me something random, just remember that I've willingly participated in plenty of our nonsense, too. I'm not exactly an innocent party here.

Sometimes, talking about absolutely nothing is still a way of spending time with someone. And I'm glad I've gotten to spend some of that time with you.

title: The Day I Sent You Your-Debt
body:
Hahaha, I still wonder what went through your mind when I sent you the Your-Debt website. Like, out of all the things I could make, why did I decide to make a whole website about debt? Bintahi.

I can already imagine you opening the link and wondering what kind of nonsense I had made this time. A normal person might send a message or make a simple joke, but apparently, I decided that wasn't enough. I had to turn the joke into an actual website.

Honestly, I don't even know what reaction I was expecting from you. Maybe you'd laugh, maybe you'd question my sanity, or maybe you'd just think, "What is wrong with this guy?" All of those would be reasonable reactions, to be fair.

But that's one of the funny things about being friends with me. Sometimes, a random idea enters my head, and before you know it, there's an entire website waiting in your messages. You never really know what I'm going to make next.

Anyway, I hope you found it funny. And don't worry, this notebook isn't a collection agency. You can read in peace. Hahaha.

title: The Little Things I Remember — Chapter 1
body:
What was your craving checklist again?

You said you wanted a burger, so I treated you to an Extreme Burger. You didn't like having onions on it, and you didn't want too much sauce either. I even remember us talking about the mustard sauce. You didn't like that one, did you?

It's funny how I still remember all those little details.

It's just a burger, after all. Nothing particularly special about it. But somehow, I remember what you wanted, what you didn't like, and the little things you mentioned along the way.

I guess some details just stay with you, even when you don't realize you're keeping them.

title: The Little Things I Remember — Chapter 2
body:
I wonder if you even remember that conversation as clearly as I do.

Maybe for you, it was just another time we talked about food and what you felt like eating. Nothing worth remembering for long.

But here I am, still remembering the onions, the sauce, and that little conversation about mustard. It's ridiculous how the smallest details can stick around in your head without asking permission.

My brain forgets plenty of useful things, but apparently your burger preferences have secured a permanent place in it.

title: The Little Things I Remember — Chapter 3
body:
I think it's funny how knowing someone happens in the smallest ways.

It's not always about knowing their biggest dreams or remembering the important dates. Sometimes, it's knowing what they like to eat, what they pick out of their food, and which sauce they would rather avoid.

Little by little, you learn these things without even trying to memorize them.

Then one day, someone asks you about it, and suddenly you realize you've been paying attention all along.

title: The Little Things I Remember — Chapter 4
body:
If we ever get burgers together again, I already know a few things to keep in mind.

Less sauce. No onions. And maybe we should be careful with that mustard sauce, too. I don't need to accidentally ruin your meal after claiming I remember your preferences.

Imagine me getting the whole order right and then forgetting something completely obvious. You'd probably never let me hear the end of it.

Honestly, that sounds about right for us.

title: The Little Things I Remember — Chapter 5
body:
There's something nice about being able to remember little things about someone without making a big deal out of it.

You don't have to announce that you noticed. You don't have to turn every small memory into some grand gesture. Sometimes, you just remember because the moment stayed with you.

And when the chance comes, you use what you remember to make things a little better for them.

In this case, that meant getting you a burger the way you liked it. Nothing complicated. Just a small thing I could do.

title: The Little Things I Remember — Chapter 6
body:
So, there you have it. Somewhere in my head, there's a little list of things you like, things you don't like, and random details you probably never expected me to remember.

Your burger preferences just happen to be on that list. Congratulations, I guess. You've officially made it into the part of my brain that refuses to forget oddly specific information.

I can't promise I'll remember absolutely everything. My memory isn't that impressive, and you know I can be ridiculous sometimes.

But if you tell me the little things that matter to you, there's a chance I'll remember them long after the conversation is over.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 1
body:
And then, after that, I bought you Jollibee.

You said you wanted spaghetti, so I got you Chickenjoy with spaghetti, a mango pie, and a drink. A whole little meal, just for you.

And somehow, you managed to spill half of your drink. I still remember that part. Out of everything that happened that day, that little accident somehow found its way into my memory and stayed there.

I don't even know if you remember it the same way I do. Maybe it was just an ordinary moment for you, something that happened and was forgotten once the day moved on.

But for some reason, I can still picture it. The food, the drink, and that little bit of chaos in the middle of an otherwise ordinary day.

I guess memories don't always need to be grand or perfectly planned to become memorable. Sometimes, all it takes is a meal together and a drink that doesn't quite make it to where it was supposed to go.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 2
body:
I still find it funny that I remember something as simple as you spilling your drink.

It's not exactly the kind of memory people would usually write down. Nobody would look at that moment and think it was something worth keeping forever. It was just a little accident, nothing serious.

But somehow, those are the kinds of things I remember about spending time with you.

Not just what we ate or where we went, but the small things that happened in between. The unexpected moments that made an ordinary day feel a little more personal.

Maybe that's what happens when you genuinely enjoy someone's company. You start remembering the details without even trying, including the ones that probably shouldn't be as memorable as they are.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 3
body:
Your order was pretty specific, too.

You wanted spaghetti, and somehow the meal ended up being Chickenjoy, spaghetti, mango pie, and a drink. I hope you enjoyed all of it, even if the drink didn't survive the experience in one piece.

Looking back, it makes me smile because the memory isn't really about the food itself. It's about that little moment we shared around it.

I could probably forget what I ate that day. I might even forget a few other details if you asked me about them now.

But somehow, I remember what you wanted and what happened afterward. Apparently, my brain decided that a spilled drink was important information and filed it away permanently.

Useful? Debatable. Memorable? Definitely.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 4
body:
I think there's something comforting about memories like this.

They remind me that spending time with someone doesn't have to be extraordinary to matter. We don't always need a special occasion, an expensive place, or some perfectly planned activity to make a day worth remembering.

Sometimes, it's just buying someone their favorite food, sharing a little time together, and watching an ordinary moment turn unexpectedly chaotic because half a drink ends up somewhere it shouldn't.

It's a small thing, really. But when I think back on that day, I don't remember it as just another meal.

I remember it as a moment with you. And maybe that's why it stayed with me.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 5
body:
If we ever have another Jollibee day, I'll probably remember to keep the drink somewhere safe.

Maybe I'll even watch you a little more closely when you pick it up. Not because I'm expecting another spill, but because I already know how these ordinary moments can turn into stories I'll end up remembering later.

And if you do spill it again, I'll probably laugh about it eventually. I might tease you a little, too, depending on how dramatic the situation gets.

But honestly, I wouldn't mind having another day like that. Another meal, another random conversation, another memory that seems insignificant at first but somehow stays with me.

The drink can be replaced. The food can be bought again. But the exact little moments we share are never going to happen in quite the same way twice.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 6
body:
Maybe one day, we'll look back on these little memories and laugh at how much I managed to remember.

The burger with no onions and not too much sauce. The conversation about mustard. Then the Jollibee meal with Chickenjoy, spaghetti, mango pie, and that drink you somehow managed to spill.

None of those things would sound particularly important to someone else. They're just food orders and small accidents, the kind of details that usually disappear as time passes.

But they're part of the little collection of memories I have of you. And I think that's what makes them special to me.

I don't remember every single thing perfectly, and I'm sure there are plenty of moments I've already forgotten. But the ones that stay with me remind me that I was there, spending time with you, sharing ordinary days that turned out to mean more than I expected.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 7
body:
There's a reason I keep bringing up these tiny details.

It's not because I think every little thing we do needs to become a story. And it's definitely not because spilling a drink is some grand life event that deserves its own celebration.

It's because when I remember these moments, I remember how it felt to spend that time with you. I remember the simple happiness of being able to treat you to something you wanted and getting to share a little piece of the day with you.

Maybe you didn't think much of it at the time. Maybe you barely remember what happened after you finished eating.

That's okay. You don't have to remember every detail the way I do.

I'm just glad I got to be part of those moments. Even the messy ones.

title: The Day We Had Jollibee — Chapter 8
body:
So, yes, I remember the Jollibee meal. I remember the Chickenjoy, the spaghetti you wanted, the mango pie, and the drink that lost half its contents along the way.

It's a strangely specific collection of details to keep in my head, but here we are.

Maybe that's just how memories work. Some moments fade no matter how hard we try to hold on to them, while others stay for reasons we can't quite explain. They don't have to be life-changing. They don't even have to be particularly impressive.

Sometimes, they're just little moments with someone who matters to you.

And when I think about that day, I don't just remember of what got spilled.

Honestly, I'd take another ordinary day like that. I'll just make sure the drink has a safer journey this time.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 1
body:
Then we ordered pizza.

I remember asking you if you had eaten, and you told me you were starving because you hadn't even eaten yet. Somehow, you had been going through the day like everything was perfectly normal while your stomach was probably begging you to find something to eat.

Looking back, I really did end up feeding you a lot that day.

First, there was Jollibee. Then we got pizza, too. At this point, I was starting to wonder if my role had quietly changed into making sure you didn't go hungry.

I'm not complaining, though. It's just funny to look back and realize how many of our little memories involved food.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 2
body:
The part that gets me is how casually you told me you were starving.

You hadn't even eaten yet, and there you were, just going through the day as if it were nothing unusual. Meanwhile, I was finding out that you had been hungry this whole time.

I don't know if you were used to skipping meals or if the day had simply gotten away from you. I just remember being surprised that you hadn't eaten anything yet.

I guess that's one of those small things you learn about someone without planning to. You ask a simple question, get an unexpected answer, and somehow the conversation becomes another memory you keep.

And apparently, your hunger that day was memorable enough for me to write about it.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 3
body:
Thinking about it now, I probably should have asked you about food sooner.

You were starving, and I was only finding out when I asked if you had eaten. It's funny how something so basic can slip your mind when you're caught up in everything else happening around you.

Still, once I knew you hadn't eaten, it made sense to get you something. Nobody should have to spend an entire day running around on an empty stomach if there's a way to fix it.

And so, pizza became part of the day, too.

I don't remember every little detail about the order, but I remember the reason behind it. You were hungry, and we ended up getting food together. Sometimes, that's all a memory needs.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 4
body:
It's funny how food became such a big part of that day.

There was Jollibee, with the Chickenjoy, spaghetti, mango pie, and the drink you managed to spill. Then there was pizza, because apparently one meal wasn't enough to cover all the hunger that had been quietly building up.

But the short version leaves out the details I actually remember. The things you wanted to eat, the things that happened while we were eating, and the little conversations that came with all of it.

Those are the parts that make the day feel like ours instead of just another date on the calendar.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 5
body:
I wonder if you remember telling me you were starving.

Maybe it was just a passing comment for you. You answered my question, we figured out what to eat, and then the conversation moved on to something else.

For me, though, it became one of those details I can still recall when I think about that day. Not because it was dramatic, but because it was so ordinary and so unexpectedly funny in hindsight.

You were hungry enough to say you were starving, and somehow you had just been carrying on with your day. Meanwhile, I ended up being part of the solution by helping make sure you got something to eat.

I guess feeding you became an unplanned side quest that day. Not exactly the kind of mission I expected, but one I didn't mind completing.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 6
body:
Looking back, I really did end up making sure you had plenty to eat that day.

Jollibee first, then pizza. When I think about it all together, it sounds like I spent a good part of the day making sure you weren't hungry anymore.

Maybe that sounds like a small thing, and it is. Buying food isn't some extraordinary act. People do it every day, and there's no need to turn every meal into a grand gesture.

But I think the little things can still mean something without having to be dramatic. Sometimes, caring about someone looks as simple as asking if they've eaten and doing something about it when they say they haven't.

It wasn't a plan I made ahead of time. It just happened naturally, one moment at a time.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 7
body:
Maybe that's why I remember so much about what we ate that day.

It's not really about the Jollibee or the pizza. It's about the moments attached to them. Asking if you'd eaten. Finding out you were starving. Getting food and realizing, afterward, just how much of the day had revolved around making sure you had something to eat.

I didn't sit there thinking I was creating memories. I was just spending time with you, doing ordinary things, and letting the day happen.

But now, when I look back, those ordinary things are exactly what I remember.

It's strange how a day can feel simple while you're living it, then become a collection of little moments you want to keep.

title: The Day We Had Pizza — Chapter 8
body:
If I had to sum up that part of the day, I'd probably say this: you were hungry, we got food, and somehow I still remember it all.

The details might not seem important to anyone else. Asking whether you'd eaten isn't an extraordinary conversation, and ordering pizza isn't exactly a rare event.

But memories don't always follow a sensible ranking system. My mind apparently decided that your hunger, the food we got, and the fact that I ended up feeding you several times that day were all worth keeping.

Maybe it's because I enjoyed being there with you. Maybe it's because the little things become meaningful when they're connected to someone you care about.

Whatever the reason, I'm glad I remember it. It gives me another small piece of that day to look back on, smile at, and keep here in these pages.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 1
body:
Do you remember that time your brother brought you lunch, but you didn't like the dish he brought?

You told me you didn't eat pakbet. You explained that you actually ate some vegetables, just not that particular one. I still remember how you made that distinction, as if you needed to defend your case against vegetables in general.

Somehow, that little conversation ended with us swapping lunches.

I bought you Chickenjoy and ice cream, then took your lunch instead. Looking back, it was such a random arrangement, but we went along with it anyway.

And honestly? Your food was delicious. A little spicy, sure, but I somehow managed to finish all of it.

I still remember that whole lunch swap. What started as you not liking your food turned into one of those unexpected moments I ended up keeping in my memory.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 2
body:
I still find it funny that all of this happened because you didn't want to eat pakbet.

You weren't saying you hated every vegetable in existence. You made it clear that you ate some vegetables, just not that one. Somehow, I remember that part, too.

It's a very specific detail to keep in my head, but apparently my brain has decided that your food preferences deserve their own little archive.

Then again, I guess that's what happens when you spend time with someone. You start learning the small things about them, even the things that come up in the middle of an ordinary lunch.

I didn't expect that conversation to turn into a lunch exchange, but it did. And now, here I am, writing about it like the world's most unnecessarily detailed lunch historian.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 3
body:
The actual deal was pretty simple.

You didn't want your lunch, so I got you Chickenjoy and ice cream. In exchange, I took the food your brother had brought for you.

When I think about it now, I realize how casually we ended up doing that. There was no big plan behind it. You had food you didn't want to eat, I got you something else, and suddenly we were trading meals as if this were a perfectly normal arrangement.

I wasn't expecting anything in return beyond making sure you had something you actually wanted to eat. But your lunch turned out to be delicious, so I can't exactly say I lost that deal.

The food was a little spicy, though. I remember that clearly. Somehow, I kept eating until there was nothing left.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 4
body:
Your lunch surprised me.

I knew you didn't want to eat it, but I didn't expect to enjoy it as much as I did. It was a little spicy, and I probably noticed that with every few bites, but somehow it was still delicious enough for me to finish everything.

It's funny how food works like that. Something one person doesn't want can turn out to be exactly what someone else enjoys.

You got the Chickenjoy and ice cream you wanted, and I got a meal that turned out to be better than I expected. In the end, both of us got something out of the arrangement.

I wonder if you remember how that lunch tasted as clearly as I do. Or if you mostly remember getting your Chickenjoy and ice cream while I happily took care of the food you didn't want.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 5
body:
I think the reason I remember that lunch so well is that it wasn't just about the food.

It was the whole sequence of little things. Your brother bringing you lunch. You explaining that you didn't eat pakbet, even though you were fine with some other vegetables. Us somehow deciding to swap meals. Me buying you Chickenjoy and ice cream, then discovering that your lunch was actually really good.

Each part was ordinary on its own. Nothing about it was particularly extraordinary.

But put them all together, and suddenly it's a memory I can still tell you about in detail.

Maybe that's why I like remembering days like that. They remind me that the moments we keep aren't always the ones we plan. Sometimes, they're the random little situations that happen when we're simply spending time together.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 6
body:
Looking back, I probably should have expected that we'd somehow turn a simple lunch into a whole story.

You didn't like the food, so we found a solution. You got Chickenjoy and ice cream, and I got to try the meal your brother had brought for you. It was a pretty fair exchange, if you ask me.

The best part is that I don't remember it as some grand act of kindness. I remember it as something we just did. I wanted you to have something you liked, and I didn't mind eating what you didn't want.

And then the food turned out to be delicious, which made the whole arrangement even better for me.

I guess some memories stay with you because they show how easy it can be to do a small thing for someone without making a big deal out of it.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 7
body:
There's something amusing about how many food-related memories I seem to have with you.

The burger with no onions and not too much sauce. The Jollibee meal and the drink you spilled. The pizza after you told me you were starving. And now, the lunch your brother brought that you didn't want because it had pakbet.

At this point, someone might assume our entire friendship revolves around deciding what you should eat. Honestly, looking at the evidence, I can't completely blame them.

But I think the food is only part of the reason these moments stay with me. It's the conversations, the little surprises, and the way one ordinary situation leads into another.

I wasn't trying to collect memories that day. I was just there with you, and somehow the details stayed.

title: The Day We Swapped Lunches — Chapter 8
body:
If you ever forget that lunch, let me remind you of the important details.

You didn't want to eat pakbet. You clarified that you still ate some vegetables, just not that one. We ended up swapping lunches. I bought you Chickenjoy and ice cream, and I took the food your brother had brought for you.

Then I discovered that your lunch was actually delicious, even if it was a little spicy. And somehow, I managed to finish all of it.

It's such a simple memory, but I can still picture the whole thing when I think about it.

Maybe I'll forget a few details someday. Maybe the exact taste of the food won't stay with me forever. But for now, I remember that lunch swap, and it makes me smile.

I guess that's enough of a reason to keep it here.

title: A Work in Progress
content:
This notebook isn't finished yet, and I don't think it needs to be.

There are still stories I haven't written, conversations I might remember later, and little moments that haven't found their way onto these pages. Sometimes, I remember something days after it happens and think, "I should've written that down."

I want this notebook to hold more than just the big memories. I want it to include the random things we talked about, the funny moments we still laugh about, and the ordinary days that became stories worth keeping.

I might add a new page tomorrow, next week, or whenever another memory comes back to me. There's no strict order to everything, and not every page has to be perfect. I'm just putting these memories together one at a time.

So, if you come back to this notebook and find something new, that's probably why. There's always another story I haven't told yet, another little detail I remembered, or another moment I decided deserved a place here.

For now, I'll leave this page as it is. The notebook can wait for the next story, and I'll write it when I'm ready.
